title: Predictive hit budgeting and safe rollout for KV prefix policies
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Produce an operational playbook and automated tooling that predicts per-prefix hit budgets, recommends TTL and key-normalization rules, and provides a safe apply/rollback path for KV prefix cache policy changes. Scope: hit-rate projection model, synthetic workload replay for validation, config apply modes (dry-run, shadow, staged canary), rollback triggers and dashboarding. Excludes kernel-level runtime changes — integration only with existing KV cache service and routing layer.
acceptance_criteria: A1: A reproducible hit-rate projection script that, given a 7-day query histogram, outputs per-prefix expected hit_rate, expected token savings, and 95% confidence intervals.
A2: Automated key-normalization recommendations (collation rules) that reduce cold-key cardinality by >= 20% on a flagged customer trace in staging.
A3: New apply modes implemented: dry-run, shadow (mirror reads), and staged canary (traffic split), with orchestration via rollout API.
A4: Dashboard panels (prefix histogram, hit_rate, tokens_saved, error_rate, tail_latency) wired and updating within 5 minutes of rollout start.
A5: Rollback automation triggers that will revert a staged policy if tokens_saved < projected_by_40% or 95th latency increases by >15% for 5 consecutive minutes.
A6: Playbook documented with step-by-step rollback and post-mortem checklist and linked PRs and runbooks.
updates: 2026-02-12: Kickoff meeting with SRE, Runtime, and Console. Agreed model inputs: per-prefix request counts, average response length, previous TTLs. Action: collect 7d histograms from bigtable export.
2026-02-18: Prototype projection script committed. Uses exponential TTL decay assumption + Poisson arrivals. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-tooling/pull/128
2026-02-25: Discovered high cardinality due to timestamp suffixes. Implemented normalization rules: strip ISO timestamps, collapse numeric IDs when appropriate. Test trace reduced cardinality by 34%.
2026-03-03: Shadow mode implemented in KV proxy; mirror reads enabled for canary namespace. Integration tests green. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kv-proxy/pull/4123
2026-03-09: Dashboard prototype added to Console application and accessible at /console/dashboards/kv-prefix-rollouts. Small bug in rate-aggregation fixed (PR 4141).
2026-03-12: Added rollback trigger definitions and end-to-end test in staging. Starting first customer pilot next week (customer alpha).
monitoring_queries: tokens_saved_per_min = sum(original_tokens - served_from_origin_tokens) where served_from_cache = true
rollout_plan: Step 0: Dry-run report generation against 7d historical traces and present to PM/SE for approval.
Step 1: Shadow apply in staging for 48h with mirror reads enabled (no writes), collect metrics and compare to projection.
Step 2: Staged canary in one small customer namespace (2% traffic) for 30 minutes, observe metrics.
Step 3: Ramp to 10% traffic for 1 hour if metrics within thresholds, then 50% for 2 hours, then 100%.
Step 4: Full apply and monitor 24h with extended alerts for 95th latency and error rate.
Each stage must have a documented rollback window and a responsible engineer on-call.
rollback_triggers: Trigger A: Actual tokens_saved < 60% of projected tokens_saved in the last 10 minutes.
Trigger B: 95th latency increases by >15% relative to baseline for 5 consecutive minutes.
Trigger C: Error rate for KV reads increases above 0.5% sustained for 2 minutes.
Trigger D: Any customer complaint flagged by support with severity >= P1 during rollout.
notes: Modeling trade-offs: simple decay + Poisson gives fast, explainable estimates. We will evaluate a secondary ML-based estimator if projection errors >20% in initial pilots.
Key-normalization decisions must be conservative: avoid over-collapsing keys that could create hot prefixes. Add opt-out annotations for critical keys.
Safety: prefer shadow mode for customers with strict correctness requirements; apply only after manual review for high-value customers.
Operational cost: projected monthly token savings for pilot customer ~ 12% (estimate, depends on workload).
Follow-ups: add a feature to automatically suggest prefix splits when TTL tuning would otherwise create hotspots.
